title: This Portal clone is created with 10 prompts under 30 min.
author: shottycoin
selftext: Everybody talks about gpt-image-2 , I have more impressive show than that. This Portal clone is created under 30 min. I didnt except it to create these Portal effects (camera mirroring and particles) but it did. Portal Gun and Cube are ready-made assets from Sketchfab. Will change it with AI Generated models too just to make it fully AI Gen.

replies.author: Undecided_Username_

Eh, listen I agree with the sentiment of it sucks when people steal ideas in a plain and obvious way, but this is a post of a guy screwing around with AI. 

I have some creative work I make that has already been stolen as quick as I started advertising it, but that’s the nature of the world, theres assholes out there thay are gonna steal your ideas. The thing is, my ideas were all derivative of other people’s ideas, so I can’t even be that mad about my idea being stolen, I can only take it as motivation to be better and to be innovative. If I’m lucky, I’ll succeed regardless, but there’s a very real chance someone wholly steals my idea and even does it better than me. 

You’ve gotta compete with the reality of the situation, not an idealistic rendition where everyone is operating under best moral practices.

To be fair, a lot of good games don't actually do anything unique and new, they just do existing things well, or combine existing things in an interesting way.

I do think there's a danger in that we need people with expertise to keep pushing and doing new things, and we might lose that if everyone relies on AI to do all the work.

replies.author: AMadHammer
replies.body:
Yeah and I think that is where posts would capture my attention. There are plenty of games that tried to iterate on the portal idea by mixing it with other concepts to make something new. 


I see game development as cooking with ingredients. Mixing two concepts can yield something new. And every once in a while a new "flavor" is discovered and people realize that now they have to make a Dubai chocolate fusion out of everything and some of those would work out. 


I just wish the posts here were bringing new fusions to show us new ideas than showing us capabilities that are the equivalent of downloading an open source game or engine template.

comments.author: rollinff
comments.body:
The challenge with posts like these and many others I've seen on X or YT, it's always about how quickly AI can get to a reasonable clone of an established game.

The technology is incredibly impressive, but the unspoken implication is that it could also, in 30 mins or 1 prompt or whatever, create a new game, a game of the quality of Portal or Minecraft, just as easily! Which is nowhere close to true. It clones well because it has the games to model after. Many reading this understand that but I really don't think most do.
